<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

Introduced `findMachineStatusCondition(machine, conditionType)` which returns a normalized `{Status, Reason, Message}` or `nil` if absent. Controllers now use it in place of the prior CAPI lookup: missing `MachineNodeHealthy` marks machines as not healthy (aggregated under `WaitingForNodeRefReason`), and missing `Ready` marks machines as not ready (aggregated under `WaitingForInfrastructureFallbackReason`). Ready condition messages are appended only when non-empty and not matching setup-counter patterns. Aggregation now sorts per-reason messages deterministically and enforces per-reason and global message-length caps with truncation suffixes. Tests were added/expanded to cover lookup, aggregation, ordering, and truncation behaviors.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Controller as NodePoolController
  participant API as MachineAPI
  participant Finder as findMachineStatusCondition
  participant Aggregator as aggregateMachineReasonsAndMessages
  participant NP as NodePoolStatus

  Controller->>API: list Machines
  API-->>Controller: Machines[]
  loop for each Machine
    Controller->>Finder: findMachineStatusCondition(machine, conditionType)
    Finder-->>Controller: {Status, Reason, Message} or nil
  end
  Controller->>Aggregator: aggregateMachineReasonsAndMessages(per-machine results)
  Aggregator-->>Controller: aggregatedReasons, aggregatedMessage (truncated)
  Controller->>NP: set NodePool conditions (Healthy/Ready) with aggregated info
  NP-->>Controller: status updated
```

</details>

<!-- walkthrough_end -->

Here it is: # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced - **Build ID**: 2046939246891110400 - **Target**: e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced - **Failed Tests**: TestCreateCluster/ValidateHostedCluster, TestAutoscaling/ValidateHostedCluster - **PR**: openshift/hypershift#8247 ([CNTRLPLANE-2204](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-2204): improve AllNodesHealthy and AllMachinesReady conditions) ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` util.go:3023: Failed to wait for HostedCluster to have valid conditions in 10m0s: context deadline exceeded eventually.go:225: observed *v1beta1.HostedCluster invalid: controlPlaneVersion state is Partial, expected Completed ``` ### Summary Both TestCreateCluster and TestAutoscaling failed identically: HostedClusters rolled out successfully (nodes ready, CVO completed, all operators available) but the new `controlPlaneVersion` status field remained stuck at `Partial` instead of transitioning to `Completed`. The blocker is the `cluster-network-operator` ControlPlaneComponent, which is the **only** component out of ~37 with `RolloutComplete=False`. It fails because the v2 CNO component reconciler unconditionally checks for the `cloud-network-config-controller` deployment when `NetworkType=OVNKubernetes`, but this deployment is never created on KubeVirt platforms — it only exists on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack). **This is a pre-existing bug in the v2 control-plane-operator framework, not caused by PR #8247's NodePool condition changes.**
Root Cause The root cause is a platform-awareness bug in `control-plane-operator/controllers/hostedcontrolplane/v2/cno/component.go`, specifically in the `checkOperandsRolloutStatus()` function. **The bug**: When `NetworkType == OVNKubernetes`, the function adds `cloud-network-config-controller` to its list of required operand deployments to verify. However, `cloud-network-config-controller` is only deployed on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack) where cloud-specific network credentials exist. KubeVirt does not deploy this controller, so the check permanently fails with: ``` failed to get deployment cloud-network-config-controller: Deployment.apps "cloud-network-config-controller" not found ``` This causes the `cluster-network-operator` ControlPlaneComponent to report `RolloutComplete=False` with reason `WaitingForOperands`. Since the `controlPlaneVersion` field requires ALL ControlPlaneComponents to have `RolloutComplete=True` before transitioning from `Partial` to `Completed`, the HostedCluster is stuck forever. **Why both tests failed identically**: Both TestCreateCluster and TestAutoscaling create KubeVirt-based HostedClusters, so both hit the same CNO rollout check bug. The CVO (old version tracking) completed successfully (`status.version.history[0].state: Completed`), but the new `controlPlaneVersion` field (used by the E2E validation) remained at `Partial`. **PR #8247 is NOT the cause**: The PR modifies only NodePool condition logic (`AllNodesHealthy`, `AllMachinesReady`). ControlPlaneComponent rollout status is computed independently of NodePool conditions — it depends solely on deployment availability in the hosted control plane namespace.
Recommendations 1. **Fix the CNO rollout check**: Add platform-awareness to `checkOperandsRolloutStatus()` in `control-plane-operator/controllers/hostedcontrolplane/v2/cno/component.go`. Only check for `cloud-network-config-controller` on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, IBMCloud), not on KubeVirt, Agent, or None platforms. 2. **PR #8247 can be retested**: This failure is unrelated to the NodePool condition improvements. A `/retest` should be attempted after the CNO fix lands, or the job can be considered a known flake for this platform combination. 3. **Check if other KubeVirt e2e jobs are affected**: Any KubeVirt job that validates `controlPlaneVersion` reaching `Completed` will hit this same failure. The older `status.version` (CVO-based) check passes because it doesn't depend on ControlPlaneComponent status. 4. **There is a partial fix in progress** (commit 1f4b7c931) that skips OVN deployment checks when `NetworkType=Other`, but this does not cover the KubeVirt case where `NetworkType=OVNKubernetes`. The fix needs to be extended to also check the platform type.
